test_title: PYST 53: SSC CPO - General Knowledge and General Awareness (Held on 04 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution empowers the Parliament to restrict or abrogate the fundamental rights of the members of the armed forces, para-military forces, police forces, intelligence agencies and analogous forces?
solution:
The Correct Answer is __Article 33.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 33 of the Indian Constitution grants Parliament the authority to modify the application of certain fundamental rights to specific groups, ensuring the proper discharge of their duties and the maintenance of discipline.
 
• These groups include members of the Armed Forces, forces responsible for public order maintenance, personnel engaged in intelligence or counterintelligence activities, and individuals involved with telecommunication systems related to these entities. Parliament holds the prerogative to restrict or abrogate these rights as deemed necessary.
 
• It's important to note that laws enacted under Article 33 are exclusive to the Parliament of India, and state governments do not possess the authority to legislate in this regard.
 
• Furthermore, any legislation passed under Article 33 cannot be challenged in court on the basis of violating fundamental rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Article 35 of the Indian Constitution vests Parliament with exclusive authority to enact laws pertaining to Articles 16(3), 32(3), 33, and 34. Additionally, it empowers Parliament to establish penalties for offenses related to fundamental rights.
 
• Article 31 of the Indian Constitution was repealed and substituted by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1978.
 
• Article 37 of the Constitution of India pertains to the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP). These principles serve as guidelines for the state to adhere to while formulating new policies and procedures.
